note:
The GEMM tiles and MNNVL one-shot collectives this capture runs that the ported GLM-5.2 spec-5 set does not name.

None of these rules names a tile. Enumerating tiles was the first attempt and it does not converge: cuBLAS picks a different `nvjet_*` variant per layer shape, and this capture alone shows more than thirty of them across six operations, with the same variant serving two different operations in different layers. `name` is a substring predicate, so `nvjet_` plus the *operation* of a neighbour is both shorter and stronger evidence -- it is the cost manifest's slot order, which is the one authority on what a decoder layer's GEMMs are.

Several rules can only fire after another has run: the GEMM feeding a split-K reduction is identified by the reduction, and the reduction is identified by what *it* feeds. That is three sweeps deep for the router. The driver must therefore run this file, `target_rules.json` and `target_extra_rules.json` to a joint label-state fixpoint rather than once each.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: fused Q and latent KV projection
rules.note: The layer's first GEMM: the fused norm-and-rope that consumes it is the next position.

rules.name: cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel
rules.role: fused Q and latent KV projection
rules.note: The ported file has this rule keyed on `attention.normalization_and_rope`, which is what GLM-5.2 called the operation; GLM-5.3 calls it `attention.main_rope`, so the ported rule matches nothing here.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: fused Q and latent KV projection
rules.note: Fires only after the rule above has labeled the reduction: the split-K GEMM is two positions from the rope, so its own neighbour is the reduction and not the rope. Both neighbour predicates are given because `before` alone would also admit the non-split GEMM the first rule already owns.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: query up projection

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: DSA indexer key-weight projection
rules.note: Only the two `full_index` families own an indexer; the `index_share` families reuse a previous layer's top-k.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: attention output projection
rules.note: A GEMM immediately in front of a reduction is o_proj at the ATTENTION reduction only. The earlier form of this rule stated that uniquely, on the grounds that the expert block reduces after an elementwise and the embedding after the vocabulary gather -- but it missed the dense layers, whose FFN down_proj is also a GEMM sitting directly in front of a reduction. Naming the permitted predecessor is what restores the uniqueness, so the rule is split once per predecessor rather than relying on file order to out-run the down_proj rule. This variant covers the absorbed decode path, where the value up-projection feeds it.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: shared-expert gate and up projection
rules.note: The activation between the two projections is what identifies this one; the three dense layers run the same pair as their FFN, which is why the dense suffix is listed.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: BF16-to-FP32 router GEMM assembly; vLLM fuses FP32 output conversion into the GEMM
rules.note: Third sweep: the reduction above names the GEMM that feeds it. Leaving this pair unmapped is what made `moe.router` read 0.0012 ms measured against 0.444 ms simulated.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: BF16-to-FP32 router GEMM assembly; vLLM fuses FP32 output conversion into the GEMM
rules.note: The non-split-K case: the router GEMM sits directly in front of the gate/up projection. `before_name` is what keeps it there. The shared expert's own gate/up GEMM is also an `nvjet_` whose successor carries this operation -- but that successor is the split-K REDUCTION, not the GEMM. Without the name test this rule reaches across and claims the shared expert's GEMM, and because apply() takes the first matching rule in file order and then stops, it does so ahead of the corrective overwrite rule further down, which then never runs. Requiring the successor to be a GEMM separates the two cases with no ordering assumption.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: shared-expert down projection
rules.note: The projection the activation feeds. The dense suffix is listed for the same reason as on the gate/up rule: this capture's activation kernel does not distinguish a dense layer's FFN from a sparse layer's shared expert, so one operation owns both slot names.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: fused Q and latent KV projection
rules.note: vLLM does not always emit the A projection as one GEMM: in most layers of this capture the Q and latent-KV halves are two back-to-back `nvjet_*` launches between the previous layer's reduction and the norm-and-rope. The manifest has exactly one GEMM slot in that span, so both launches are it.

rules.name: vllm::rotary_embedding_kernel
rules.role: DSA indexer rotary embedding
rules.note: The indexer's own rope, immediately after its query projection. The main path's rope is fused into `_fused_norm_rope_kernel` and is a different kernel entirely.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: projection of the six collected target hidden states down to the draft width
rules.note: The draft phase's first GEMM, ahead of vLLM's DFlash2 input preparation, and the manifest's first draft slot. Its measured 87.4 ms against the slot's 93.4 ms simulated is consistent with that reading, but the position is what the label rests on.

rules.name: FillFunctor<unsigned char>
rules.role: sparse MLA input preparation: the query concatenation, the latent KV cache append and the sparse index remap
rules.note: One operation for three positions, deliberately, because the evidence supports the span and not the order inside it. Every sparse-MLA attention launch in this capture is preceded by exactly three positions -- `FillFunctor<int>`, a kernel whose name the profile lost, and `FillFunctor<unsigned char>` -- and the cost manifest has exactly three leaves in that same span: `query_concat`, `mla_cache_append` and `index_remap`. What is NOT established is which measured kernel is which leaf: two of the three are generic ATen fills whose names say nothing about their role, so pairing them off in order would be a guess dressed as a reading. Comparing the three together against the three leaves together is the strongest claim the capture actually supports.

rules.name: kernel
rules.role: sparse MLA input preparation: the query concatenation, the latent KV cache append and the sparse index remap
rules.note: Pinned by both neighbour names rather than by a chain: the bare fragment `kernel` is a substring of nearly every measured name, so a chain keyed on it would walk backwards out of this span.

rules.name: FillFunctor<int>
rules.role: sparse MLA input preparation: the query concatenation, the latent KV cache append and the sparse index remap

rules.name: cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel
rules.role: shared-expert gate and up projection
rules.note: `overwrite` because this position is claimed twice across rule files and the other claim is wrong. The decode sequences fold the expert block into a four-position body -- gate/up GEMM, split-K reduction, activation, down projection -- whose first position has no predecessor at all, and a chain of `attention.fused_qkv_a_proj` rules reaches it from the other side and labels both GEMM and reduction as the attention A projection. The consequence is visible in the numbers: before this rule `moe.shared_expert.gate_up_proj` read 2.0 ms measured against 183.6 ms simulated on the decode iterations while reading +3.6% on the mixed ones, which is not a model error but 450 positions labeled as a different operation. `label check` cannot see this: it reads final labels, and the two claims live in different files, so no single `apply` ever sees them together.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: shared-expert gate and up projection
rules.note: The GEMM the reduction above reduces.

rules.name: cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel
rules.role: fused Q and latent KV projection
rules.note: When the first half of the A projection is split-K its reduction lands between the two halves. `before_name: nvjet_` is load-bearing and not decoration: without it this rule also matches the reduction that feeds the shared expert's activation, which is the gate/up projection's and not this one's.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: tensor-parallel language-model head projection
rules.note: The head runs on the rows a gather has just selected, which is the only place in the sample phase a GEMM follows a gather. Keyed on the predecessor's name because the gather itself is unmapped -- it is vLLM's last-token selection and the model folds it into the head.

rules.name: cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel
rules.role: tensor-parallel language-model head projection

rules.name: CatArrayBatchedCopy
rules.role: DSA indexer key/query preparation and top-k selection: the quantisations, the key layernorm, the weight scale, the index cache append and the top-k buffer fill
rules.note:
One operation for the whole span between the indexer's rope and `q_absorb`, for the same reason `attention.sparse_mla.preparation` is: the bracket is evidence, the order inside it is not. The span holds eleven unmapped positions and the manifest holds eleven indexer leaves between those two anchors, but the measured members are a `CatArrayBatchedCopy`, a run of generic ATen elementwise kernels and one attention kernel, none of whose names says which leaf it is.

The bracket does settle one thing that was open before. `fmhaSm100aKernel_QkvBfloat16OBfloat16H256SeparateQkvCausalVarSeqQ128Kv` was left unlabeled on an earlier pass because it could not be placed: it is not the DSA MLA kernel, which is `fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16HQk576HV512...`, and it sits before `q_absorb`, which the manifest puts ahead of the main attention. With both anchors labeled it is inside the indexer block, so it is an indexer kernel, and `indexer.prefill_logits` is the only attention-shaped leaf in the span. That pairing is not what this rule asserts and nothing here depends on it -- the claim is the span.

`slot_suffixes` lists only the indexer leaves no other operation already claims. Adding the ones the name-keyed rules own -- `prefill_logits`, `decode_logits`, `decode_topk`, `prefill_cache_gather` -- would count their simulated time twice.

rules.name: CatArrayBatchedCopy
rules.role: DSA indexer key/query preparation and top-k selection: the quantisations, the key layernorm, the weight scale, the index cache append and the top-k buffer fill
rules.note: The same span in the layers whose indexer ran the decode top-k, where that kernel rather than the rope is the last labeled position before it.

rules.name: elementwise_kernel
rules.role: DSA indexer key/query preparation and top-k selection: the quantisations, the key layernorm, the weight scale, the index cache append and the top-k buffer fill
rules.note: Chains along the run. It cannot walk out of the span: `q_absorb` closes it and is a GEMM, which this name fragment does not match.

rules.name: CatArrayBatchedCopy
rules.role: sparse MLA input preparation: the query concatenation, the latent KV cache append and the sparse index remap
rules.note: The query concatenation itself, which is the first thing after the absorb and was outside the three positions this operation started with.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: draft vocabulary projection feeding the candidate selection
rules.note: The GEMM whose split-K reduction the rule above already names.

rules.name: fmhaSm100aKernel
rules.role: sparse MLA attention
rules.note:
The MLA prefill attention, on the path where vLLM does not absorb: no `q_absorb` and no `v_up` run in these layers, the query and key are materialised at head dim 256, and the kernel is plain causal variable-length FlashAttention rather than the DSA kernel. Two things settle it. The bracket: it is the last position before `attention.o_proj`, and the manifest has only the attention between the indexer and the output projection. And the companions: `ComputeLSEFromMDKernel` and `merge_attn_states_kernel` run beside it, which is the chunked prefix merge and belongs to nothing else.

It was left unlabeled on two earlier passes because the DSA kernel is `fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16HQk576HV512...` and this one looked like a different family -- which it is, but of the same operation. `Sm100a` versus `Sm100f` is the tell, and the name alone is enough to separate them.

rules.name: nvjet_
rules.role: DSA indexer MQA logits over the prefill query rows
rules.note: On the prefill path the index logits are a cuBLAS GEMM rather than the `deep_gemm` kernel the name-keyed rule owns. Same operation, different implementation: it is the only GEMM between the indexer's key concatenation and the masking run that selects from its output.

rules.name: elementwise_kernel
rules.role: DSA prefill top-k selection
rules.note: The selection the logits feed, which the capture runs as a run of ATen comparisons, bitwise operations and binary functors rather than one kernel. Bracketed by the logits GEMM behind it and the attention in front of it.

rules.name: elementwise_kernel
rules.role: DSA prefill top-k selection

rules.name: elementwise_kernel
rules.role: sparse MLA input preparation: the query concatenation, the latent KV cache append and the sparse index remap
rules.note: On the decode path the preparation run starts right after the indexer's top-k, which is the last labeled position before it, and is longer than the three positions this operation started from.

rules.name: elementwise_kernel
rules.role: sparse MLA input preparation: the query concatenation, the latent KV cache append and the sparse index remap
rules.note: Chains along that run. The attention closes it and is not an elementwise kernel.
